items.q: What is Wheatley's mistake about the Christies of the world?
items.a: We want the hard conversation, then **put all the courage on the giver**. Too many barriers for that to happen consistently. **Receivers** have to make it safer and **lower the courage required**. Don't wait — ask someone who cares *and* will be honest if you make it cheaper.

items.q: What did his sister's silence already tell him?
items.a: Work said he can sound arrogant. She paused: **"Yeah."** She had needed him and **did not call because of that tone**. Loved ones may already be voting with withdrawal. The missing feedback was not a lack of people who cared.

sections.title: Name the thing, cue it live

items.q: What is 'your thing,' and what was his?
items.a: **Everyone has a thing** — a not-at-your-best move you often cannot hear. His: arrogant, condescending, self-righteous, know-it-all. Christy's (with permission): **0 to 100 in about two seconds**, then something she regrets.

items.q: What beat a book or a training?
items.a: He asked for a course. She said she'd just tell him. Cue: **"You're doing your thing"** when he started with **"Well, actually."** First time he had to cue *her* while she was already upset, he was terrified; she cooled off and thanked him.

items.q: Why does 'How am I doing as your manager?' fail?
items.a: Everyone says **"Great!"** It is too scary. Narrow it: *"I want to get better at running our staff meetings. What's **one** piece of advice?"* Titles are a second barrier — Christy assumed the loop died when he became her boss. Re-authorize out loud.

**Thankfulness** (calm fight-or-flight: *that wasn't easy to hear, glad you said it*) → **Acknowledgment** (seen/heard first; you need not agree; defense shuts them down) → **Commitment** (change, more perspectives, or a dated callback) → **Thankfulness again** (text or handwritten card so it was **worth the risk**).
